meta.title: Size of the chewing gum market in India

prompt: Estimate the size of the chewing gum market in India (annual revenue).

clarifications.answer: Assume consumption below 15 and above 50 is negligible, and ignore the lower-income half of the population.
A packet holds four units of gum and costs about Rs 5; assume 50 buying-weeks in a year.
Use an age-wise split, and within each age band split consumers by frequency (packets per week).
Express the market size in crore rupees per year.

common_traps: Treating the whole population as consumers instead of restricting to ages 15-50 and the upper half of income.
Using one flat consumption rate rather than splitting each age band by frequency (heavy/medium/light).
Mixing up packets and units, or forgetting to convert weekly consumption into a 50-week year.

anchors.1: Guesses a market size with no consumer-times-frequency-times-price structure.
anchors.3: Uses consumers x packets x price but with one blanket consumption rate.
anchors.5: Builds consumers x packets-per-year x price and derives packets-per-year from an age-and-frequency split.

anchors.3: Segments by age only, with a single consumption rate per band.
anchors.5: Segments by age and, within each band, by frequency of consumption.

anchors.1: Loses track of crore conversions or lands far from any plausible figure.
anchors.3: Reaches a number with a slip, landing just outside 6000-10000 crore.
anchors.5: Carries the weekly-to-yearly and crore math cleanly, landing near 8000 crore.

anchors.1: States the number as final with no check.
anchors.3: Mentions a check but does not complete it.
anchors.5: Cross-checks per-capita spend: ~8000 crore over ~35 crore consumers is a plausible few-rupees-per-week habit.
